newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices end mixed.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices end mixed.

text.p: Cotton prices were mixed on Tuesday on the local market where demand was limited to quality varieties, traders said.
They said the varieties from the western state of Gujarat were higher on a shortage of ready stock while those from the northern Punjab region remained steady.
Traders said the quality of Punjab cottons at end of the 1996/97 season (October/September) was generally poor.
"We have to depend on Gujarat cotton for our immediate needs," one trader said.
In spot, Gujarat Kalyan rose 100/500 rupees to 15,000/15,200 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) and Wagad gained 100/200 rupees at 13,600/13,700 rupees per candy.
Punjab saw-ginned was steady at 1,830/1,900 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) and so was Bengal-deshi at 1,125/1,160 rupees and F-414 at 2,080/2,100 rupees per maund.
